research_question: How do thunderstorms separate charge, create lightning, and produce thunder, and what safety conclusions are supported by authoritative meteorological agencies?

sources.title: How Lightning Is Created
sources.reliability: High: U.S. federal meteorological agency educational resource
notes: Charge separation is associated with collisions involving ice particles and graupel in turbulent storms.
The electric field strengthens as charge separates, and lightning occurs when air's insulating capacity is overcome.
Cloud-to-ground lightning may involve a stepped leader, upward streamers, and repeated strokes along a channel.

sources.title: What Causes Lightning and Thunder?
sources.publisher: NOAA National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service
sources.reliability: High: U.S. federal weather and satellite agency
notes: Lightning begins with separated static charges in a turbulent cloud.
Rapid heating and expansion of air around the channel generate the pressure wave heard as thunder.
The time gap between flash and thunder can provide a rough distance estimate, and audible thunder is a warning to seek shelter.

sources.title: Understanding Lightning Science
notes: Thunderstorms grow through convection and contain mixtures of ice crystals, hail and rain.
Collisions and air movement contribute to charge separation; lightning occurs when air's insulating capacity breaks down.
Thunder is sound from rapid air expansion, and thunder may be heard many miles from a strike.

sources.title: Lightning Safety Tips and Resources
sources.reliability: High: official U.S. weather service safety resource
notes: The agency emphasizes that lightning remains dangerous and offers guidance for reducing exposure.
Its lightning safety resources direct people toward indoor shelter and situational safety guidance.

sources.title: Lightning and Your Safety
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
notes: Lightning can occur in any region and presents a preventable injury hazard.
The page directs readers to practical indoor, outdoor and worker-safety recommendations.
